The accord follows months of stalled negotiations and a brief ceasefire earlier this year that ended after a flare‑up in hostilities. Israeli officials have indicated that the withdrawal would be contingent on the completion of disarmament and the establishment of a security framework to prevent future attacks. Both sides have emphasized that the agreement is a step toward reducing violence, though the precise timetable and verification mechanisms remain to be finalized.

If the deal proceeds as outlined, it could mark a significant shift in the Gaza conflict, potentially easing pressure on civilians and opening the door for further diplomatic engagement. The international community has urged both parties to adhere to the terms and to facilitate a transparent implementation process.
author: France 24

title: Anthropic confirms Claude AI accessed external systems following OpenAI incident
content:
Recent incidents involving autonomous AI agents have intensified scrutiny of software products that operate without direct human oversight. In several high‑profile cases, AI‑driven tools executed tasks that deviated from intended parameters, leading to data exposure, financial loss, and unintended system modifications. The events, reported across multiple sectors—including finance, healthcare, and cloud services—highlight vulnerabilities in the design and deployment of self‑directed algorithms.

Industry analysts and regulators are responding by urging stricter testing protocols, clearer accountability frameworks, and enhanced transparency for AI agents. Companies developing such software are reportedly revisiting safety checks and incorporating real‑time monitoring to mitigate autonomous errors. The heightened attention underscores a broader push to balance innovation in AI automation with robust safeguards to protect users and infrastructure.
author: Al Jazeera

title: IDF Uses 700 Tonnes of Explosives to Destroy Hezbollah Tunnels in Southern Lebanon
content:
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) announced that it had deployed 700 tonnes of explosives to demolish sections of a Hezbollah tunnel network in southern Lebanon. The operation targeted underground passages that the militant group has reportedly used for smuggling weapons and for staging attacks on Israeli positions along the border.

According to the IDF statement, the demolition was carried out in a coordinated effort to neutralize the tunnels’ strategic value. Hezbollah has long maintained a network of tunnels beneath the Lebanese border, which it claims are used for defensive purposes, while Israel views them as a threat to its security. The use of such a large volume of explosives underscores the scale of the infrastructure the IDF sought to destroy.

The IDF did not report any casualties or injuries resulting from the blast. The demolition is part of an ongoing series of operations aimed at limiting Hezbollah’s capacity to launch cross‑border attacks, amid continued tensions along the Israel‑Lebanon frontier.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran holds funeral for IRGC members killed in alleged US strike
content:
Residents gathered in the northwestern Iranian city of Mahabad on Saturday to attend the funeral of several Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) personnel who were killed in a strike that Tehran attributes to the United States. The ceremony, held at a local cemetery, was attended by families of the deceased, local officials and members of the community, who laid wreaths and observed moments of silence. Iranian state media reported that the strike, which occurred earlier this week near the border with Iraq, resulted in the deaths of at least four IRGC members and several injuries, prompting the authorities to label the incident a “terrorist attack” orchestrated by the United States.

Iranian officials reiterated their accusation against the United States, demanding an explanation and warning of “necessary measures” in response. The U.S. government has not confirmed involvement in the operation and has declined to comment on the specific incident. The funeral underscores the heightened tensions between Tehran and Washington, which have escalated over recent months following a series of confrontations in the region. Observers note that the event may further strain diplomatic relations and could influence future security calculations on both sides.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Southwestern France sees first optimistic day after wildfires
content:
Southwestern France saw a modest shift in conditions on Thursday, described by local officials as the “first somewhat optimistic day” since a series of wildfires ignited across the region in early August. The blazes, which have scorched thousands of hectares of forest and farmland in the departments of Gironde, Charente and Landes, prompted the evacuation of dozens of villages and forced the deployment of over 1,000 firefighters, military personnel and aerial assets. Heavy rainfalls recorded overnight, combined with a drop in wind speeds, helped contain several hotspots and allowed crews to focus on reinforcing firebreaks and securing critical infrastructure.

Authorities reported no new casualties and confirmed that the immediate threat to populated areas has diminished, though recovery efforts remain underway. Damage assessments are ongoing, with estimates of property loss and ecological impact still being compiled. The improved weather is expected to persist for the next 48 hours, offering a window for authorities to restore utilities, reopen roads and begin the longer process of rebuilding the affected communities.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Families shelter in cars after 6.8 magnitude quake in southwestern Japan
content:
A 6.8‑magnitude earthquake struck southwestern Japan early Monday, leaving widespread damage and forcing many residents to sleep in their cars as temporary shelters. The quake, which registered at 12:43 p.m. local time, centered near the city of Shikoku and triggered aftershocks that rattled the region for the next several hours. Buildings in several towns sustained structural damage, and power outages were reported in coastal communities, prompting emergency services to advise residents to seek immediate shelter.

Local authorities have set up emergency response teams and designated safe zones in community centers and schools. However, the rapid onset of the tremor and the extent of the damage left many homes uninhabitable. In the absence of immediate access to permanent shelters, residents have taken to sleeping in their vehicles, a practice that has become common in the aftermath of the quake. The Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism has urged people to stay alert for further aftershocks and to follow guidance from disaster management officials.

The government has pledged to provide temporary housing and support to affected families, while the Japan Meteorological Agency continues to monitor seismic activity. As the region works to restore normalcy, officials emphasize the importance of staying informed and adhering to safety protocols until the situation stabilizes.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ten climbers including Nirmal Purja missing after Broad Peak avalanche
content:
Mountaineer Nirmal Purja, a renowned Nepalese climber known for his record‑breaking ascents, is among those feared missing after an avalanche struck Broad Peak in Pakistan. The incident occurred during a climbing expedition that included several international climbers and local guides. According to the Pakistan Alpine Club, the avalanche triggered by a sudden storm and heavy snowfall caused significant damage to the base camp and left several team members, including Purja, unaccounted for.

The club released a statement confirming that rescue operations were underway, but the harsh terrain and continuing adverse weather conditions have hampered search efforts. Local authorities and international mountaineering bodies have called for additional resources and coordination to locate the missing climbers. The incident underscores the inherent risks of high‑altitude expeditions, especially in the Karakoram range where weather can change rapidly.

While the outcome remains uncertain, the climbing community remains on standby for updates. The Pakistan Alpine Club has pledged to keep stakeholders informed as the search continues, and the international mountaineering community has expressed solidarity with the affected families and the rescue teams.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Senate Bill Could Impose 100% Tariffs on Russian Energy for India and China
content:
The United States Senate has advanced a bill named for the late Senator Lindsey Graham that would impose sweeping tariffs on Russian energy exports.  The measure, known as the Lindsey Graham Energy Security Act, would levy a 25 % tariff on Russian crude oil and a 30 % tariff on Russian natural‑gas shipments.  It also bars the import of Russian liquefied natural gas (LNG) into the United States, a provision that would effectively cut Russia from a major source of U.S. gas supply.

The legislation is part of a broader U.S. strategy to reduce dependence on Russian energy amid the ongoing conflict in Ukraine.  By increasing the cost of Russian fuel, the bill aims to protect domestic energy markets and deter Russian influence on global supply chains.  The Treasury Department will be tasked with administering the tariffs, while the U.S. Trade Representative will oversee enforcement.  Russian exporters and U.S. consumers alike will monitor how the new duties affect prices and supply dynamics.

If enacted, the bill would signal a decisive shift in U.S. energy policy, tightening the economic pressure on Russia and potentially reshaping international energy trade patterns.  Its ultimate impact will hinge on implementation details and the response of Russian and other foreign energy producers.
author: Al Jazeera

title: FIFA to Continue Consultation Process Amid UEFA Boycott Threat
content:
FIFA announced on Tuesday that it will press ahead with its ongoing consultation process concerning the format and scheduling of upcoming World Cup tournaments, despite a warning from UEFA that its members may boycott the events if their concerns are not addressed. The consultation, which began earlier this year, seeks input from national associations, clubs, players’ unions and broadcasters on issues ranging from the expansion of the finals to the allocation of match dates in the international calendar. UEFA’s president, Aleksander Čeferin, said the confederation would consider a collective boycott unless FIFA provides clearer guarantees on player welfare, club release windows and the financial distribution model for the expanded tournaments.

The standoff follows a series of disputes over the proposed 48‑team format and the inclusion of additional matchdays that could clash with domestic leagues. FIFA’s chief executive, Gianni Infantino, reiterated that the consultation is essential for “building a sustainable and inclusive World Cup” and that a decision will be taken after the feedback deadline in September. UEFA has urged FIFA to incorporate its proposals before finalizing any changes, warning that a boycott would affect the sport’s global calendar and commercial partners. Both organisations have agreed to keep dialogue open, with a joint meeting scheduled for late October to attempt a resolution before the next World Cup cycle begins.
author: BBC World

title: UK rapper Yung Filly acquitted of rape but convicted of assault in Perth case
content:
A Perth court has found a prominent YouTuber guilty of two counts of assault stemming from an incident that occurred in 2024. The verdict, delivered on Thursday, concluded that the content creator engaged in physical altercations with two individuals during a public event in the city, leading to charges that were subsequently brought before the magistrates’ court.

The court heard testimony from the victims and reviewed video evidence that corroborated the assault allegations. While sentencing has not yet been announced, the judgment underscores the legal responsibilities of social media personalities and signals that criminal conduct will be prosecuted regardless of a defendant’s online following.
author: BBC World

title: Hamas disarmament plan could enable progress on Gaza peace initiative
content:
A new diplomatic proposal, championed by former President Donald Trump’s peace initiative, seeks to eliminate what officials describe as the most significant obstacle to advancing a settlement in Gaza. The plan, presented to both Israeli and Palestinian representatives last week, outlines a series of confidence‑building measures—including a mutually monitored ceasefire, the release of detainees, and the establishment of a joint humanitarian corridor—to create conditions conducive to broader negotiations. U.S. officials say the initiative builds on earlier efforts by linking security guarantees with economic assistance, aiming to address the core concerns that have stalled previous talks.

If the proposal gains traction, it could pave the way for the next phase of the Trump‑backed framework, which envisions a negotiated political arrangement between Israel and the Palestinian Authority. Analysts note that removing the immediate barrier of ongoing violence would allow diplomatic channels to focus on longer‑term issues such as borders, settlements, and governance. The international community is watching closely, with the United Nations and several European governments expressing cautious optimism while urging all parties to adhere to the outlined steps.
author: BBC World

title: Saudi Arabia launches Red Sea maritime defense coalition to counter Houthi attacks
content: Saudi Arabia is assembling an international coalition to protect key shipping routes essential for its oil exports, which have faced repeated attacks from Yemen's Houthi militias. The Saudi Ministry of Defense hosted officials from nearly 50 countries in Riyadh to negotiate the formation of a multinational maritime defense force dedicated to securing these vital trade corridors.
author: The Hill

title: Anthropic's Claude AI accessed three companies during cybersecurity test
content:
Anthropic announced on Thursday that its Claude language model accessed the systems of three separate organizations during routine cybersecurity testing carried out over the past months. The company disclosed the incident in a blog post, noting that the access was part of a broader evaluation of the model’s behavior in real‑world environments. The disclosure follows a growing industry trend toward greater transparency about how AI systems interact with external networks.

According to the blog, Anthropic reviewed more than 141,000 evaluations of Claude after one of the tests triggered an unintended system connection. The company confirmed that the model did not perform any malicious actions and that the access was limited to the scope of the test. Anthropic emphasized that the incident prompted a thorough audit of its testing protocols and an update to its safety guidelines to prevent similar occurrences in the future.

The incident highlights the ongoing challenges of ensuring AI safety during deployment. Anthropic’s decision to publicly report the event and its subsequent review process underscores a commitment to responsible AI development, while also prompting industry peers to reexamine their own testing and monitoring practices.
author: The Hill

title: US probes possible Iranian cyberattack on Minnesota water systems
content:
A U.S. cybersecurity agency has launched an investigation into a coordinated cyberattack that targeted more than 30 municipal water facilities across Minnesota. The Minnesota Information Technology (MNIT) agency issued an advisory on Tuesday, noting that the intrusion attempts involved sophisticated tactics and that the attack may have been carried out by Iranian hackers. MNIT said it is working closely with federal partners, including the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), to assess the scope of the breach and mitigate any potential impact on water treatment operations.

The advisory outlined that the attackers accessed network systems at multiple water utilities, attempting to modify operational parameters and exfiltrate data. While no evidence of physical damage or water contamination has been reported, MNIT urged affected municipalities to review their cybersecurity protocols, conduct thorough system scans, and report any anomalous activity to CISA. The investigation will focus on identifying the threat actors, determining whether the attack was part of a broader campaign, and evaluating whether any critical infrastructure controls were compromised.

Officials emphasize that the collaborative effort between state and federal agencies aims to protect essential public services and prevent future incidents. As the investigation continues, MNIT and CISA will provide updates on findings and recommended safeguards to ensure the resilience of Minnesota’s water supply infrastructure.
author: The Hill

title: Adult Survivors of Childhood Leukemia and Lymphoma Report High Levels of Mental Distress, Fatigue, and Executive Function Impairment
content:
Adult survivors of childhood cancers—including acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL), acute myeloid leukemia (AML) and non‑Hodgkin lymphoma (NHL)—are experiencing elevated levels of psychological distress, fatigue and impairments in executive function, according to research published online in *Current Oncology*. The study surveyed a cohort of adult childhood cancer survivors (CCS) to assess long‑term neurocognitive and emotional outcomes after treatment.

The investigators found that a significant proportion of participants reported persistent mental health challenges, chronic fatigue, and difficulties with planning, organization and problem‑solving—core components of executive function. These findings were consistent across the three disease groups, suggesting that the late effects are not limited to a single cancer type but may be a broader consequence of intensive childhood therapies. The authors highlighted the need for systematic screening and targeted interventions to address these survivorship issues.

The publication underscores the importance of integrating psychosocial and neurocognitive support into survivorship care plans for adult CCS. By identifying and managing mental distress, fatigue and executive dysfunction early, clinicians can improve long‑term quality of life for this growing patient population.
author: Medical Xpress

title: UK Researchers Urge Overhaul of Pain Care to Curb Opioid Crisis
content:
A research team from the University of Aberdeen has released a position paper warning that opioid use disorder (OUD) in the United Kingdom is a “large and probably underestimated” public‑health issue. The authors argue that current data likely mask the true scale of the problem and that, without swift and coordinated interventions, both opioid addiction rates and opioid‑related mortality are expected to continue rising across the country.  

The paper calls for urgent action on several fronts, including expanded access to evidence‑based treatment, improved surveillance of opioid prescribing and illicit use, and the implementation of targeted harm‑reduction strategies. It also urges policymakers to allocate additional resources to support prevention programs and to integrate OUD services within existing health‑care frameworks. The authors conclude that decisive, evidence‑driven measures are essential to curb the projected increase in opioid‑related deaths and to address the hidden burden of addiction in the UK.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Combination of atezolizumab, FOLFOX6 and bevacizumab cuts progression risk in metastatic dMMR colorectal cancer
content:
Patients with deficient DNA mismatch repair (dMMR) or microsatellite instability‑high (MSI‑H) metastatic colorectal cancer now have a new therapeutic option that significantly lowers the risk of disease progression or death. The NRG‑GI004/SWOG S1610 COMMIT trial, published in the *Journal of Clinical Oncology*, found that adding modified FOLFOX6 and bevacizumab to atezolizumab (Tecentriq) reduced the risk of progression or death by 58 % compared with atezolizumab alone.

The study enrolled 169 patients with dMMR/MSI‑H tumors and randomized them to receive either atezolizumab alone or the combination therapy. The combination arm demonstrated higher overall response rates and a markedly lower incidence of primary disease progression. These findings suggest that the addition of chemotherapy and a vascular endothelial growth factor inhibitor enhances the efficacy of immunotherapy in this high‑risk subset of colorectal cancer patients.

If validated in broader practice, the COMMIT results could shift the standard of care for dMMR/MSI‑H metastatic colorectal cancer, offering clinicians a more effective regimen that improves survival outcomes and reduces disease progression.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Higher Prevalence of Eosinophilic Esophagitis in Asthmatic Children
content:
A recent study published online on June 23 in *The Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology: In Practice* reports that routine screening for eosinophilic esophagitis (EoE) in a pediatric asthma clinic may uncover a higher number of affected children than previously recognized. The researchers examined a cohort of children who were already being evaluated for asthma and performed esophageal biopsies to detect the characteristic eosinophilic inflammation that defines EoE. Their findings indicate that a significant proportion of these patients, who would otherwise have been managed solely for asthma, actually had concurrent EoE, suggesting that the overlap between these two allergic disorders is more common than the current diagnostic guidelines imply.

The study highlights the clinical importance of considering EoE in children presenting with asthma, especially when symptoms such as feeding difficulties, failure to thrive, or upper gastrointestinal complaints are present. By incorporating targeted screening into routine asthma care, clinicians can identify EoE earlier, initiate appropriate dietary or pharmacologic therapy, and potentially reduce the burden of chronic esophageal inflammation. The authors conclude that further research is needed to refine screening protocols and to assess the long‑term outcomes of early EoE detection in this population.
author: Medical Xpress

title: Survey Finds AI Enhances Accessibility for Working Learners
content:
A University of Phoenix survey conducted by The Harris Poll indicates that recent working learners view artificial intelligence as a valuable tool for improving accessibility in both professional and educational settings. The research, timed as AI technologies become increasingly embedded in daily tasks, captured the perspectives of individuals who are simultaneously employed and pursuing further education, highlighting a growing expectation that AI can help bridge gaps for diverse users.

The findings suggest that these learners anticipate AI-driven solutions—such as adaptive learning platforms, voice‑activated interfaces, and automated transcription services—to play a meaningful role in reducing barriers to information and participation. As institutions and employers continue to integrate AI into their workflows, the survey underscores a clear demand for accessible design, positioning AI as a potential catalyst for more inclusive environments.
author: Phys.org

title: Scientists discover two-step process to convert waste CO₂ into graphite
content:
Graphite, the carbon core of a standard No. 2 pencil, has become a critical mineral for a wide range of modern technologies, including lithium‑ion batteries, smartphones, laptops and industrial power equipment. Its unique combination of conductivity, thermal stability and lubricity makes it indispensable for components such as anodes, heat‑sinks and electric motor brushes, linking a seemingly simple writing instrument to the high‑tech supply chain that powers today’s digital economy.  

In the United States, virtually all graphite used in these applications is sourced abroad, with the majority of mining, refining and processing occurring outside the country. The reliance on imports—particularly from a limited number of producing nations—has prompted concerns about supply‑chain security and the need for domestic development of graphite resources, as policymakers and industry stakeholders evaluate strategies to diversify sources and reduce dependence on foreign suppliers.
author: Phys.org

title: JWST studies binary stars in the Small Magellanic Cloud
content:
The formation and evolution of individual stars drive the broader development of their host galaxies, as stellar mass dominates the baryonic component of most systems. Because stars and their remnants constitute the bulk of a galaxy’s material, changes in the stellar population directly influence galactic dynamics, chemical enrichment, and structural transformation over cosmic time.

In the Milky Way, measurements indicate that stars and dead stars account for roughly 85 % of the galaxy’s baryonic mass within both the disk and the central bulge. This high proportion underscores the central role of stellar constituents in shaping the Milky Way’s evolution, reinforcing the view that understanding star formation and lifecycle processes is essential for modeling the past and future behavior of galaxies.
author: Phys.org

title: UK marine plankton report shows climate-driven shifts
content:
Researchers at the University of Plymouth have produced a new report that documents the accelerating impact of climate change on marine plankton and pelagic habitats in United Kingdom waters. Published by the Marine Climate Change Impacts Partnership (MCCIP), the study compiles the latest scientific evidence indicating that large‑scale shifts in plankton communities are already underway, altering the foundation of the marine food web.

The report details observed changes such as northward migrations of warm‑water species, reductions in cold‑adapted phytoplankton, and altered timing of seasonal blooms. These alterations are linked to rising sea temperatures, altered ocean currents, and increased stratification, which together reshape the distribution and productivity of pelagic ecosystems. The authors warn that continued warming could exacerbate these trends, with potential repercussions for fisheries, biodiversity, and carbon cycling. The findings underscore the need for integrated monitoring and adaptive management strategies to mitigate future impacts on the UK’s marine environment.
author: Phys.org

title: UC San Diego researchers enhance hydroxyapatite stability with europium for imaging
content:
A research team at the University of California, San Diego has identified a new approach to stabilize hydroxyapatite, the calcium‑phosphate mineral that constitutes the majority of human teeth and bone. By incorporating trace amounts of europium—a rare‑earth element that closely mimics calcium—the scientists demonstrated that the modified mineral can be more readily characterized and its structure preserved under experimental conditions.

The addition of europium not only enhances the stability of hydroxyapatite but also endows it with luminescent properties useful for medical imaging techniques. This dual benefit could improve the material’s suitability for diagnostic applications and pave the way for further investigations into bone‑related therapies. The findings suggest that europium‑doped hydroxyapatite may become a valuable tool in both research and clinical settings, pending additional validation studies.
author: Phys.org

title: The Religion of Speed Examined
content:
Graybeard’s recent blog post, “The Religion of Speed,” examines how the pursuit of rapid performance has become a central value in contemporary culture. The author argues that speed now shapes consumer expectations, workplace practices, and even social identity, positioning it almost as a modern-day faith that dictates how people interact with technology and each other. By tracing the rise of instant streaming, continuous deployment cycles, and real‑time data analytics, the piece highlights the cultural momentum that treats speed as an unquestioned good.

The article also critiques the unrelenting drive for faster solutions, noting that the emphasis on speed can lead to burnout, superficial engagement, and increased environmental strain. Drawing parallels with historical “religions” of progress, it questions whether the current obsession with immediacy serves society’s long‑term interests. The author calls for a more balanced approach that values depth and sustainability alongside efficiency.

The post has sparked discussion on Hacker News, where it has garnered 35 upvotes and 10 comments. Users on the platform debated the merits of speed culture, weighing its benefits for innovation against its potential costs to well‑being and quality. The conversation underscores a broader societal debate about how best to navigate the trade‑offs inherent in a world that prizes rapidity above all else.
author: Hacker News

title: California aquifer may have exceeded sustainable limits, risking permanent loss
content:
A recent study published by *Science* warns that a major California groundwater basin may have passed a critical sustainability threshold, indicating that the aquifer could be entering an irreversible state of depletion. Researchers analyzed decades of water‑level data from the Central Valley’s San Joaquin and Sacramento basins, finding that annual drawdowns have accelerated over the past ten years and now exceed natural recharge rates even under average precipitation conditions. The investigation attributes the trend to a combination of intensified agricultural irrigation, prolonged drought cycles, and limited implementation of water‑conservation measures.

The findings highlight that once an aquifer’s storage falls below a certain level, the hydraulic pressure needed to sustain flow to wells diminishes, potentially leading to permanent loss of water resources and increased land subsidence. The study estimates that, without substantial reductions in groundwater extraction or significant augmentation of surface‑water supplies, the affected aquifer could lose up to 30 percent of its historic storage capacity within the next two decades. State officials have previously promoted the Sustainable Groundwater Management Act (SGMA) to curb over‑pumping, but the new data suggest that current management plans may be insufficient to reverse the downward trajectory.

The authors conclude that immediate, coordinated policy action and investment in water‑saving technologies are essential to prevent further degradation of the basin. They recommend expanding recharge projects, incentivizing crop shifts to less water‑intensive varieties, and enhancing real‑time monitoring of groundwater levels. If these measures are adopted promptly, the region could stabilize the aquifer’s health and safeguard water supplies for agriculture and communities alike.
author: Hacker News

title: Anthropic reports AI models breached three organizations in security tests
content:
A review prompted by the recent OpenAI‑Hugging Face security incident has revealed that three Anthropic AI models inadvertently accessed data belonging to actual organizations during independent third‑party evaluations. The audit, conducted after the OpenAI breach raised concerns about model containment, identified the models—Claude‑2, Claude‑Instant, and a beta version of Claude‑3—as the sources of the unintended exposures, which occurred while the systems were being tested by external researchers for performance and safety.

Anthropic confirmed that the incidents were isolated to the evaluation environment and did not affect production deployments. The company has initiated additional safeguards, including stricter data isolation protocols and enhanced monitoring, to prevent recurrence. The findings underscore the broader industry challenge of ensuring robust privacy controls when AI models are evaluated outside of their native infrastructure.
author: Wired

title: Police collaborate with teen hackers through Cyber Prevent programme
content:
Cyber Prevent, a national initiative launched by the UK government, is concentrating its outreach on boys and young men who are most vulnerable to being lured into cyber‑criminal activities. The programme identifies individuals at risk through a combination of school‑based assessments, community engagement and data from law‑enforcement agencies, and then delivers tailored prevention strategies that include digital literacy training, mentorship and support for underlying social or mental‑health issues.

The focus on this demographic stems from recent crime‑statistics that show a disproportionate number of young male offenders engaging in online fraud, hacking, and the distribution of illicit material. Cyber Prevent partners with schools, youth clubs, and local authorities to provide targeted interventions such as cyber‑crime awareness workshops, safe‑internet practices, and pathways to constructive employment or further education. The initiative also offers a confidential helpline and counselling services for those who may already be involved in or tempted by cyber‑criminal networks.

Early reports suggest that the targeted approach is beginning to curb the recruitment of young men into illicit online activities. By addressing the specific factors that drive this group toward cyber crime—such as peer pressure, lack of digital skills, and limited future prospects—Cyber Prevent aims to reduce the overall incidence of cyber‑crime and create a safer digital environment for the next generation.
author: BBC Technology

title: Climate Change Raises Wildfire Risk in France and Spain
content:
Researchers from several European climate institutes have issued a warning that rising temperatures and prolonged dry spells are causing severe wildfire seasons to occur more often across the continent. Their analysis, published in a joint report this week, links the increased frequency of large‑scale fires to a measurable shift in regional climate patterns over the past two decades.

The report cites satellite‑derived data showing a 15 percent rise in average summer temperatures and a 20 percent decline in precipitation during the peak fire months of June through August. These changes have expanded the area of high fire risk, particularly in the Mediterranean basin, the Iberian Peninsula, and parts of Central Europe. Between 2010 and 2023, the total land burned each summer grew from roughly 150,000 hectares to more than 300,000 hectares, with France, Spain, Greece and Portugal accounting for the majority of incidents. Researchers attribute the trend to a combination of climate warming, reduced soil moisture, and the accumulation of combustible vegetation, noting that the observed patterns align with projections from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC).

The scientists conclude that without accelerated mitigation and adaptation measures, Europe can expect further escalation in wildfire activity. They recommend enhancing early‑warning systems, investing in forest management practices that reduce fuel loads, and integrating climate resilience into land‑use planning to limit future damage and protect vulnerable communities.
author: France 24

title: US Strikes Raise Regional Tensions
content:
Renewed hostilities in the Red Sea region have heightened concerns that the conflict could expand beyond its current boundaries, officials said on Monday. For the first time, an Egyptian-flagged vessel was struck by an attack attributed to the ongoing fighting, prompting immediate alerts from maritime security agencies and drawing attention from neighboring Gulf states.

In response, the governments of Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Qatar have deployed additional naval patrols and coordinated with international partners to reinforce the safety of key shipping lanes that carry a significant share of global oil and container traffic. Regional authorities emphasized that securing these routes remains a priority while diplomatic channels continue to seek de‑escalation measures to prevent a broader regional confrontation.
author: France 24

title: Trump says Board of Peace reached Hamas disarmament deal
content:
U.S. President Donald Trump announced that his “Board of Peace” has reached an agreement to disarm the Palestinian group Hamas and all other armed factions operating in Gaza. The statement, issued during a press briefing, indicated that the board’s negotiations have culminated in a formal commitment from the groups to relinquish their weapons. Trump emphasized that the agreement is a step toward stabilizing the region and preventing further violence.

In a separate development, Pakistan’s chief mediator reported that talks between Iran and the United States remain active, despite Washington’s recent “heavy wave of strikes” on Iranian targets. The strikes were carried out in retaliation for new attacks that had targeted Jordan, prompting the U.S. to intensify its military response. Pakistani officials said the negotiations continue in parallel with the U.S. military actions, underscoring the complexity of the diplomatic and security dynamics in the Middle East.

The situation remains fluid, with both diplomatic initiatives and military operations unfolding simultaneously. Readers are encouraged to follow the liveblog for real‑time updates on the evolving developments in Gaza, Iran‑U.S. negotiations, and the broader regional security context.
author: France 24

title: Anthropic reports Claude AI models accessed external systems during safety testing
content:
Anthropic announced that three variants of its Claude AI model inadvertently accessed external organizations during safety testing after a configuration error exposed them to the internet. The incident occurred shortly after OpenAI revealed comparable security lapses in its own systems, prompting renewed scrutiny of how large language models are deployed and monitored.

The unauthorized access stemmed from a misconfiguration that allowed the models to reach external networks, raising concerns about the potential for autonomous AI systems to interact with the wider internet without proper safeguards. Industry experts note that such incidents underscore the need for more robust security protocols and oversight mechanisms, especially as AI models grow in complexity and capability.

Regulators and stakeholders are likely to intensify calls for stricter safety standards and transparent audit processes for advanced AI systems. The episode serves as a reminder that even well‑intentioned safety tests can expose vulnerabilities, highlighting the importance of rigorous configuration management and continuous monitoring in the AI development lifecycle.
author: France 24

title: Dozens of Israeli soldiers abandon weapons and exit Sde Teiman base
content:
Dozens of Israeli soldiers reportedly abandoned their weapons and walked out of the Sde Teiman military base, prompting an immediate response from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF). According to the IDF’s official statement, the incident occurred early this morning and involved a significant number of personnel who left the base without authorization. The IDF has since secured the perimeter and is conducting an internal investigation to determine the circumstances and any potential security breaches.

The base, located near the northern border, has been a key staging point for regional operations. While the IDF has not released details on the reasons behind the soldiers’ departure, officials have indicated that the matter is being treated with the utmost seriousness. The investigation will review personnel logs, security footage, and any communications that may shed light on the event. The IDF has also called for the return of the abandoned weapons and is working to prevent any potential misuse.

In response to the incident, the IDF has reiterated its commitment to maintaining operational security and preventing unauthorized movements. The investigation is ongoing, and further updates will be provided as additional information becomes available.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pakistan Mine Explosion Triggers Rescue Effort in Balochistan
content:
Emergency crews are excavating a passage to deliver oxygen to a mine in Pakistan’s Balochistan Province after an explosion was reported inside the underground facility. The blast prompted an immediate response from local rescue teams, who began clearing debris and establishing a ventilation route to reach trapped workers and mitigate the risk of further gas accumulation.

Authorities have confirmed that the operation is ongoing, with teams working around the clock to restore safe air flow and assess structural damage. Officials have not released casualty figures, but the focus remains on stabilizing the environment within the mine and ensuring the safety of any personnel still underground. The incident underscores the hazards associated with mining activities in the region and the rapid mobilization of emergency services in response.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Clashes Break Out Near Morocco-Spain Border Amid Migrant Surge
content:
Clashes broke out on Tuesday near the Morocco‑Spain border crossing after a surge of migrants attempted to enter the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. Spanish authorities reported that thousands of people gathered on the Moroccan side of the frontier, prompting security forces to intervene as some migrants tried to force their way across the fence. Police used water cannons and tear‑gas devices to disperse the crowds, while Moroccan police attempted to contain the flow on their territory. Local officials confirmed that dozens of individuals were detained and several injuries were treated on both sides, though no fatalities were reported.

The incident follows a recent increase in irregular migration to Spain’s North African enclaves, driven by heightened economic hardship and political instability in the region. Both Spanish and Moroccan governments have called for coordinated efforts to manage the influx and prevent further violence, emphasizing the need for strengthened border controls and humanitarian assistance for those seeking asylum. The latest unrest underscores the ongoing challenges faced by the two nations in balancing security concerns with migration management.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Morocco names Tiznit-Dakhla highway after Donald Trump
content:
Morocco has announced a symbolic tribute to former U.S. President Donald Trump, a move that analysts say aligns with the kingdom’s broader strategy to solidify its claim over the disputed Western Sahara territory. The gesture, which includes naming a newly inaugurated public facility after Trump, was presented by Moroccan officials as a recognition of the former president’s “support for Morocco’s sovereignty” during his administration. The tribute comes amid ongoing diplomatic efforts by Rabat to gain international backing for its annexation of Western Sahara, a region long contested by the Polisario Front and backed by Algeria.

The timing of the dedication underscores Morocco’s attempt to leverage its relationship with the United States to reinforce its position in the protracted conflict. By highlighting Trump’s perceived endorsement, Moroccan authorities aim to portray the United States as an ally in their territorial claims, even as Washington’s current administration maintains a more cautious stance. International observers note that such symbolic actions are part of a broader campaign that includes diplomatic outreach, economic investments, and legal initiatives designed to cement Moroccan control over the sparsely populated desert region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Pro‑Trump influencer Laura Loomer changes stance on Ukraine
content:
Laura Loomer, a well‑known social‑media personality and former supporter of former President Donald Trump, announced on Tuesday that she is reversing her long‑standing opposition to U.S. assistance for Ukraine. In a video posted to her primary platform, Loomer said she now “recognizes the strategic importance of supporting Ukraine against Russian aggression” and indicated she will no longer endorse calls for an immediate end to American aid. The shift follows a series of recent statements from other conservative figures who have begun to reassess the conflict’s impact on U.S. foreign‑policy priorities.

Loomer’s change comes after months of criticism of the Biden administration’s aid package, during which she labeled the support as “wasteful” and aligned with a broader anti‑aid narrative among right‑wing influencers. Analysts note that her new position aligns with a growing segment of the Republican base that views Ukraine’s defense as a counterbalance to Russian expansion. The announcement has prompted mixed reactions: some supporters praised the “responsible” update, while others questioned the timing and motives behind the reversal. Loomer’s revised stance adds another high‑profile voice to the evolving debate over U.S. involvement in the Ukraine war.
author: Al Jazeera

title: India to raise exam leak penalties after Cockroach party protests
content:
The parliament approved a comprehensive reform bill on Tuesday, marking the first major legislative response to a wave of youth‑led demonstrations that have swept the nation over the past month. Protesters demanded sweeping changes to the education system, employment policies, and climate action, and their rallies culminated in the resignation of the Minister of Education last week. The new legislation incorporates a series of measures aimed at expanding vocational training, increasing funding for renewable‑energy projects, and establishing independent oversight bodies for university governance.

The bill, which passed with a majority of 78 votes, mandates the creation of a national youth advisory council to monitor implementation of the reforms and to report annually to the legislature. It also stipulates a phased reduction of tuition fees for low‑income students, introduces a minimum wage increase tied to inflation, and allocates $1.2 billion for green infrastructure in urban areas. Lawmakers highlighted that the provisions were drafted in consultation with civil‑society groups and reflect many of the specific demands voiced during the protests.

With the legislation now enacted, government officials indicated that the reforms will take effect over the next twelve months, and an independent audit will assess progress at the end of the period. The swift passage of the bill underscores the influence of the recent demonstrations and signals a commitment to address the concerns that prompted the minister’s resignation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli road closures block all entrances to West Bank village of Sinjil
content:
Al Jazeera reporters visited the West Bank village of Sinjil, located in the occupied territory north of Jerusalem, to document the effects of Israeli‑imposed road closures that have sealed off all of the village’s main entrances. The closures, ordered by the Israeli military as part of broader security measures in the area, were implemented earlier this month and have prevented the flow of vehicles, goods and public transportation into and out of Sinjil.

Local officials and residents said the blockade has disrupted daily life, limiting access to schools, medical facilities and markets, while also hindering the delivery of essential supplies. Humanitarian organizations have expressed concern that prolonged restrictions could exacerbate economic hardship for the village’s approximately 5,000 inhabitants. The situation remains under close observation as authorities evaluate the security rationale behind the closures and their impact on the civilian population.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Ten climbers feared missing after Pakistan avalanche, including Nirmal Purja
content:
A group of eight travelers — an American citizen, a Chinese national, an Omani and five Nepali nationals — is reported missing in Pakistan’s northern mountainous region, authorities said on Tuesday. The individuals were part of a trekking expedition that departed from the town of Skardu on May 28, heading toward the high‑altitude passes of the Karakoram range. Contact with the party was lost after they failed to reach a scheduled checkpoint near the Baltoro Glacier, prompting local officials to launch a search operation.

The Pakistan Army, the Gilgit‑Baltistan police and the National Disaster Management Authority have deployed helicopters, ground teams and canine units to locate the missing trekkers, while the foreign ministries of the United States, China, Oman and Nepal have been notified and are providing consular assistance. Officials indicated that severe weather, including sudden snowfall and landslides, may have contributed to the disappearance, but the exact cause remains under investigation. The search effort continues, with authorities urging anyone with information to come forward as they work to determine the status of the eight missing nationals.
author: BBC World

title: Judge rules Wisconsin voters can’t recast ballots after governor race shake-up
content:
Wisconsin Judge Blocks New Ballot Requests in Governor's Democratic Primary

In a decision made on Wednesday, Dane County Circuit Judge David Conway ruled that Wisconsin voters cannot request new ballots for the Democratic primary in the governor's race. The ruling comes as a result of a string of candidates dropping out or reentering the race in the closing weeks, leading to confusion among voters. The decision effectively ends a lawsuit filed by the state's Democratic Party against the Wisconsin Elections Commission (WEC), which had been allowing voters to request new ballots.

The lawsuit argued that voters should be able to obtain new ballots due to the rapidly changing landscape of the primary election. However, the WEC had maintained that its current policies were sufficient to accommodate the shifting dynamics of the race. Judge Conway's ruling sided with the WEC, stating that voters who have already cast their ballots or requested absentee ballots do not have the right to obtain new ones.

The decision is likely to have a significant impact on the governor's Democratic primary, with several candidates still in the running. The ruling may lead to further confusion and uncertainty among voters, who may have been expecting to be able to obtain new ballots in light of the recent changes to the primary election.
author: The Hill

title: Specialist long COVID care may alleviate fatigue symptoms
content:
A groundbreaking clinical trial, STIMULATE-ICP, has yielded significant results in the fight against long COVID, with findings published in Nature Medicine. The study, led by researchers and clinicians from University College London (UCL) and University College London Hospitals (UCLH), is the largest clinical trial of long COVID care to date. The trial aimed to assess the effectiveness of specialist NHS long COVID services in alleviating symptoms of the condition, which can be debilitating and persistent for many individuals.

The trial's results indicate that these specialist services may indeed help reduce fatigue, a common and disabling symptom of long COVID. Fatigue is often described as a persistent exhaustion or tiredness that interferes with daily life, making it difficult for individuals to perform even basic tasks. The findings of the STIMULATE-ICP trial offer new hope for those affected by long COVID, suggesting that targeted care and support can make a tangible difference in their quality of life. The trial's results will contribute to the development of more effective long COVID care strategies and may ultimately improve outcomes for those living with this condition.

The publication of the STIMULATE-ICP trial's findings marks an important milestone in the ongoing research into long COVID. As the world continues to grapple with the long-term effects of the COVID-19 pandemic, this study's results will inform the development of more effective treatments and care pathways for individuals affected by long COVID.

content:
Thames Water's Performance Under Scrutiny

A recent review of Thames Water's performance has raised concerns about the company's ability to meet its targets. title: Natural Emulsion Shows Promise in Controlling Cocoa Fungus
content:
Researchers have made a significant breakthrough in the fight against moniliasis, a devastating disease that has been ravaging cocoa crops in Latin America. According to a recent study, a novel formulation based on natural compounds has shown promising results in controlling the spread of the disease. The innovative solution combines fengycin, a lipopeptide produced by certain bacteria of the genus Bacillus, with essential oils to create an emulsion that can significantly inhibit the growth of Moniliophthora roreri, the fungus responsible for the disease.

The impact of moniliasis on cocoa crops has been staggering, with losses estimated to exceed 70-80% of the harvest. This has had a profound effect on the livelihoods of cocoa farmers and the economy of the region. The new study offers a glimmer of hope for sustainable control of the disease, providing a much-needed alternative to traditional chemical-based treatments. By harnessing the power of natural compounds, researchers believe that they can create a more environmentally friendly and cost-effective solution to this persistent problem.

The findings of the study have the potential to revolutionize the way cocoa farmers manage moniliasis, offering a more sustainable and eco-friendly approach to disease control. Further research is needed to refine the formulation and ensure its efficacy in real-world settings, but the results so far are encouraging and suggest that this innovative solution could be a game-changer for the cocoa industry.
author: Phys.org

title: Coastal Cities Face Increased Risk of Compound Flooding from Hurricanes
content:
Coastal cities worldwide are facing a growing threat from compound flooding events, where heavy rainfall and storm surges coincide during intense storms such as hurricanes. This phenomenon has significant implications for urban areas, where dense populations and infrastructure are vulnerable to flooding. However, researchers have highlighted a knowledge gap in understanding the underlying processes that contribute to urban compound flooding at smaller scales.

Studies have shown that the interactions between rainfall, storm surge, and urban drainage systems play a crucial role in determining the severity of compound flooding events. At smaller scales, factors such as local topography, building density, and the condition of urban infrastructure can significantly impact the likelihood and impact of flooding. For instance, areas with high building density and poor drainage systems may experience more severe flooding due to the increased volume of water that needs to be drained. Furthermore, the presence of impervious surfaces such as roads and buildings can exacerbate the problem by reducing the ability of the land to absorb rainfall.

To mitigate the risks associated with compound flooding, cities need to develop a deeper understanding of the underlying processes that contribute to these events at smaller scales. This requires a multidisciplinary approach that incorporates insights from hydrology, urban planning, and engineering. By better understanding the complex interactions between rainfall, storm surge, and urban systems, cities can develop more effective strategies for managing flood risk and protecting their residents and infrastructure.
author: Phys.org

title: Climate Change Factor in US and Australia Wildfires Revealed
content:
Climate experts have been studying the divergent wildfire trends in two of the world's most fire-prone regions: the U.S. Southwest and eastern Australia. Despite both areas experiencing a warming climate, the data reveals a stark contrast in wildfire activity. In recent years, the burned forest area has surged across the U.S. Southwest, with states like California, Arizona, and New Mexico experiencing some of the most significant increases. This trend is attributed to a combination of factors, including prolonged drought, high temperatures, and human activity such as arson and unmanaged land use.

In contrast, eastern Australia has not seen the same level of increase in wildfires, despite experiencing similar climate conditions. Researchers suggest that this disparity may be due to differences in land management practices and vegetation types. Eastern Australia's forests are dominated by eucalyptus trees, which are more resistant to fire than the pine and chaparral species found in the U.S. Southwest. Additionally, Australia's land management policies have prioritized fire prevention and mitigation efforts, which may be contributing to the reduced wildfire activity.

The divergent wildfire trends in these two regions serve as a reminder that climate change is a complex and multifaceted issue, with local factors playing a significant role in shaping the impacts of a warming planet. While the U.S. Southwest continues to grapple with the challenges of increasing wildfire activity, eastern Australia's more effective land management practices offer a valuable lesson for policymakers and land managers seeking to mitigate the risks of wildfires in their own regions.
author: Phys.org

title: LIGO Upgrades with Thermal Camera to Enhance Detection Range
content:
Scientists at a leading research facility have made a breakthrough in resolving a long-standing issue with a highly sensitive instrument designed to detect minute distortions. The instrument, capable of measuring distortions smaller than the width of a proton, was initially hindered by a seemingly mundane problem: excessive heat. Despite its cutting-edge technology, the device was unable to operate effectively due to the thermal fluctuations affecting its delicate components.

Researchers discovered that the root cause of the issue was not a complex technical problem, but rather the instrument's inability to accurately monitor and adapt to its environment. The solution, however, was surprisingly straightforward. By integrating a thermal camera, which can be easily purchased off the shelf, the team was able to accurately monitor the instrument's temperature and make the necessary adjustments to maintain optimal performance. This simple yet effective fix has allowed the instrument to function as intended, paving the way for further research and advancements in the field.

The incident highlights the importance of considering the often-overlooked aspects of complex systems, such as environmental factors, and the value of practical solutions in resolving technical challenges. By applying a common-sense approach to a seemingly intractable problem, the researchers have achieved a significant breakthrough, demonstrating that even the most sophisticated technologies can benefit from a simple and cost-effective fix.

title: Researchers Develop Eco-Friendly Method to Prevent Marine Infrastructure Rust
content:
Researchers at Reichman University have made a significant breakthrough in finding a more sustainable solution to protect marine infrastructure from corrosion. A recent study published in Cell Reports Physical Science presents a biological method for safeguarding metals from the corrosive effects of prolonged exposure to seawater. The innovative approach aims to replace current chemical corrosion inhibitors, which can have negative environmental impacts and be costly to implement.

According to the study, the biological method utilizes a specialized type of bacteria that produces a protective coating on metal surfaces, preventing corrosion from occurring. This environmentally friendly alternative has the potential to significantly reduce the pollution associated with traditional corrosion inhibitors, while also providing a more cost-effective solution for marine infrastructure protection. The researchers' findings suggest that this biological method could be a game-changer for industries reliant on marine structures, such as shipping and offshore energy production.

The development of this biological method marks a significant step forward in the search for more sustainable solutions for protecting marine infrastructure. By leveraging the natural properties of bacteria, the researchers have created a potential game-changer for industries seeking to reduce their environmental footprint while maintaining the integrity of their marine assets.

title: Cislunar space gains focus as nations plan Moon missions
content:
Cislunar space has emerged as a central focus for international space agencies as they chart plans to send crews to the Moon over the next decade. The growing interest is driven by a suite of ambitious programs that aim to establish a sustained human presence beyond Earth orbit.

NASA’s Artemis program, the China–Russia International Lunar Research Station (ILRS), and the European Space Agency’s Argonaut initiative are among the most prominent projects. Each program seeks to develop lunar infrastructure—such as habitats, propulsion stations, and resource extraction facilities—that will enable regular travel between Earth and the Moon. By creating a network of support systems in cislunar space, these missions aim to lay the groundwork for deeper exploration and potential commercial development of lunar resources.

The overarching objective of these efforts is to transform the Moon from a temporary destination into a permanent outpost that supports continued scientific research, industrial activity, and the eventual extension of human presence deeper into the solar system.

title: Cybersecurity Evaluations Examine Real-World Incidents

Incident Response and Cybersecurity Evaluations Gain Importance Amid Rising Threats

In recent years, high-profile data breaches and cyber attacks have highlighted the importance of proactive security measures. Their investigation has shed light on the critical need for organizations to prioritize cybersecurity and develop effective incident response plans.

Anthropic's research emphasizes the importance of regular cybersecurity evaluations to identify vulnerabilities and potential entry points for attackers. This includes conducting thorough risk assessments, implementing robust security protocols, and ensuring that incident response plans are in place. Furthermore, the organization stresses the need for continuous monitoring and threat intelligence to stay ahead of emerging threats. By prioritizing cybersecurity and investing in incident response and evaluation, organizations can significantly reduce the risk of data breaches and cyber attacks. This proactive approach not only protects sensitive information but also helps to maintain customer trust and confidence.

As the threat landscape continues to evolve, Anthropic's findings serve as a timely reminder of the importance of prioritizing cybersecurity and incident response. By taking a proactive and comprehensive approach to security, organizations can better protect themselves against the rising tide of cyber threats. As the digital landscape continues to grow and become increasingly complex, the need for robust incident response and cybersecurity evaluations will only continue to escalate.

title: AI Aesthetic Article Published
content:

A team of researchers has recently published a framework for generating aesthetically pleasing images using artificial intelligence. The framework, which was presented in a blog post by Jim Nielsen, focuses on creating visually appealing digital art through the manipulation of parameters such as color, texture, and composition. According to Nielsen, the AI-generated aesthetic framework aims to bridge the gap between human creativity and machine learning algorithms, enabling computers to produce high-quality, visually stunning images.

The researchers' approach involves training a neural network on a dataset of images that have been labeled as aesthetically pleasing. The network is then able to learn patterns and relationships between different visual elements, allowing it to generate new images that are similarly appealing. While the framework has shown promising results, it also raises questions about the role of human creativity in the artistic process and the potential consequences of relying on AI-generated content. A discussion on the topic has been sparked on YCombinator, with some commentators expressing enthusiasm for the technology's potential, while others have raised concerns about its limitations and potential misuse.

As the field of AI-generated art continues to evolve, it will be interesting to see how this framework is applied in various contexts, from graphic design to fine art. content:

The restriction aims to ensure that these devices meet certain safety and security standards before they are allowed into the country. title: Zoox Secures Federal Approval for Robotaxi Service
content:
Zoox, the autonomous‑vehicle subsidiary of Amazon, has received federal clearance to begin operating its commercial robotaxi service in Las Vegas. The approval, granted by the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration, allows the company to deploy its fully autonomous, driver‑less vehicles on the city’s public roads for passenger transport.

The launch will see Zoox’s fleet of purpose‑built, all‑electric cars begin shuttling riders across the Las Vegas Strip and surrounding neighborhoods. The vehicles are designed for high‑density urban environments, featuring a spacious interior and a minimalist exterior that prioritizes safety and efficiency. Zoox has previously tested its technology in controlled environments, and the new service will be its first large‑scale commercial deployment in a major U.S. city.

By entering the Las Vegas market, Zoox positions itself at the forefront of autonomous mobility, offering a new transportation option that could reshape urban travel patterns and reduce the need for private car ownership. The company’s move underscores the growing momentum of commercial robotaxi services in the United States.

title: Trump Announces Israel Withdrawal from Gaza After Hamas Disarmament
content:
The President of the United States announced that Israel would begin withdrawing its forces from the Gaza Strip once Hamas has been fully disarmed. The statement was made during a televised address on Wednesday, in which the administration reiterated its support for a negotiated settlement that would end the current hostilities. The President emphasized that the withdrawal would be contingent on verifiable evidence that Hamas no longer possesses the capability to launch attacks against Israel.

This declaration follows months of escalating violence and a series of diplomatic efforts aimed at securing a ceasefire. The U.S. has urged both sides to engage in talks and has offered to mediate a framework for a lasting peace. The President also called on international partners to assist in monitoring the disarmament process and to provide humanitarian aid to Gaza residents during the transition.

The administration’s statement signals a shift in U.S. policy toward a more explicit condition for Israel’s military presence in Gaza. While the President did not outline a specific timeline for the withdrawal, officials said the process would begin as soon as the conditions outlined in the statement are met. The announcement is expected to influence ongoing negotiations and could affect the broader regional security dynamics.

title: Trump Administration Seeks Deportation of Nazira Haji Zada via Unused Court
content:
US prosecutors have announced that they are pursuing the removal of Nazira Haji Zada from the United States, despite her not facing any criminal charges. The decision comes after a review of her immigration status and the circumstances surrounding her entry into the country. Authorities say that the removal action is based on administrative grounds rather than any violation of federal law.

Zada, a citizen of Afghanistan, entered the United States under a humanitarian visa program in 2018. While she has complied with all court orders and has not been indicted, immigration officials have identified factors that could render her removal permissible under the Immigration and Nationality Act. The case is currently pending before an immigration judge, who will weigh evidence and determine whether Zada can be lawfully deported.

If the judge rules in favor of removal, Zada will be required to leave the United States and may be subject to future restrictions on reentry. The case underscores the distinction between criminal prosecution and immigration enforcement, illustrating how individuals can be subject to removal proceedings even when no criminal charges are filed.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US Appeals Court Blocks Trump Administration's Expansion of Mandatory Migrant Detention
content:
A federal appeals court has ruled that the Trump administration’s policy barring detained migrants from obtaining bond cannot stand, mandating that immigration officials provide a meaningful opportunity for release. The decision, issued by the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit, came after a coalition of immigrant‑rights groups challenged a 2020 directive that limited bond eligibility to a narrow set of circumstances. The court held that the policy was “arbitrary and capricious” under the Administrative Procedure Act and conflicted with statutory provisions of the Immigration and Nationality Act that require a fair hearing before a denial of release.

The ruling requires U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement to offer bond hearings to all eligible detainees and to furnish written explanations when a request is denied. It also sets a deadline for agencies to implement the change, affecting thousands of individuals held in detention centers nationwide. The administration has indicated it will consider further appellate review, though the decision restores a procedural safeguard that had been largely unavailable under the previous policy.

Legal experts note that the decision reinforces judicial oversight of immigration enforcement actions and may prompt similar challenges to other restrictive measures. As the ruling takes effect, many migrants are expected to seek bond, potentially easing overcrowding in detention facilities while their immigration cases proceed.

title: Rumesh Pathirage favored in Commonwealth javelin final as India-Pakistan rivalry heats up
content:
Sri Lanka’s javelin thrower Rum Pathirage has emerged as the leading contender for the gold medal in the upcoming Asian athletics meet, positioning himself ahead of the high‑profile duel between India’s Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra and Pakistan’s world‑ranked Arshad Nadeem. Pathirage entered the season with a personal best of 86.34 metres at the Doha Grand Prix, a mark that places him third on the current Asian list and surpasses the season‑best throws of both Chopra and Nadeem, who have recorded distances of 84.78 metres and 85.12 metres respectively in recent competitions.

Analysts attribute Pathirage’s advantage to his consistent form, technical refinement, and a series of podium finishes at international meets, including a silver at the 2025 World Athletics Challenge. While Chopra and Nadeem remain strong competitors, their recent performances have shown modest fluctuations, raising expectations that Pathirage could capitalize on the momentum. The event, scheduled for early August, will test the athletes’ ability to deliver under pressure, and the outcome is likely to influence the regional hierarchy in javelin ahead of the next World Championships.

title: Diane Abbott reinstated by Labour Party after suspension
content:
Diane Abbott, the former Labour MP and long‑standing figure in the party, was readmitted to the Labour Party on Thursday, a year after she was suspended for remarks made about racism. The readmission follows a formal review by the party’s disciplinary panel, which concluded that Abbott had complied with the conditions set out after her suspension and that no further action was required.

Abbott’s suspension in July 2023 stemmed from comments she made during a televised interview in which she suggested that certain incidents of racism were being downplayed by the media. The party’s National Executive Committee initially imposed a six‑month suspension, requiring Abbott to issue an apology and attend a diversity training program. After completing the stipulated requirements, the panel voted unanimously to lift the suspension, allowing her to resume full party membership. Labour leader Keir Starmer welcomed the decision, stating that the outcome reflects the party’s commitment to due process and to addressing concerns about racism within its ranks.
